mainTopic: How יין נסך forbids mixtures, when a stream of it is nullified bit by bit, and when water in a wine pit can nullify it.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the previous discussion: one version says רבה בר רב הונא himself drank from a קנישקנין. A new משנה then teaches that יין נסך forbids a mixture of its own kind (wine in wine, water in water) in any amount. A mixture of a different kind (wine in water, water in wine) is forbidden only if the forbidden liquid adds taste. רב דימי reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that יין נסך poured from a barrel into a cistern of kosher wine is nullified bit by bit as it falls in. The גמרא defends this against the משנה by reading the whole משנה as permitted liquid falling into forbidden liquid. רב יצחק בר יוסף reports the rule differently: it works only with the thin stream of a small canteen, not a barrel. רבין then reports that if water also falls into the wine pit, we ignore the permitted wine, and the water, if it is more, nullifies the forbidden wine. Two versions of רב שמואל בר יהודה's teaching disagree about whether the water must fall in first. The amud ends by setting up a new איתמר about this same case, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Another version: רבה בר רב הונא drank from a קנישקנין himself
steps.stepSummary: An alternate report says רבה בר רב הונא himself drank from a קנישקנין, closing the previous discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רבה בר רב הונא himself drank from a קנישקנין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the story from the previous discussion. In this version, רבה בר רב הונא himself drank from the קנישקנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An 'איכא דאמרי' gives a different report of the same event. Saying he drank from it himself is a stronger sign that he held this vessel to be permitted. This line wraps up the earlier topic before the new משנה begins.

keyTerms.meaning: Himself
A drinking vessel discussed in the previous section

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rabba bar Rav Huna himself
drank from a kenishkanin.
phrases.notes: This is the same drinking vessel the גמרא was just talking about in the previous section.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate version of the story that ended the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, רבה בר רב הונא personally drank from the קנישקנין.

steps.title: משנה: same-kind mixtures forbidden in any amount, different-kind only by taste
steps.stepSummary: יין נסך is forbidden and forbids a mixture in any amount. Wine in wine and water in water are forbidden in any amount. Wine in water and water in wine are forbidden only if the forbidden liquid adds taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wine poured for idol worship is forbidden, and even a tiny bit of it forbids what it mixes with. Wine into wine or water into water forbids in any amount. Wine into water or water into wine forbids only if you can taste it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches how much יין נסך it takes to forbid a mixture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes two cases. When the forbidden liquid falls into the same kind of liquid, even the smallest amount forbids everything. When it falls into a different kind, it forbids only if it gives the mixture a noticeable taste (נותן טעם).

keyTerms.meaning: Wine poured as an offering to idols
Forbidden itself, and makes other things forbidden
In any amount, even the tiniest
Gives taste: forbids only if its flavor can be noticed

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Libation wine is forbidden
and renders a mixture forbidden in any amount;
wine in wine, and water in water,
phrases.notes: Water poured out for an idol is forbidden too, just like the wine.

phrases.english: in any amount;
wine in water, and water in wine,
only when it imparts flavor.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ יֵין נֶסֶךְ אָסוּר וְאוֹסֵר בְּכׇל שֶׁהוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same-kind mixtures of יין נסך are forbidden in any amount. Different-kind mixtures are forbidden only when the forbidden liquid adds taste.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for mixtures of יין נסך that the גמרא will now examine.

steps.title: משנה's general principle: same kind in any amount, different kind by taste
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up: a substance mixed with its own kind forbids in any amount, and with a different kind only by taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: same kind with same kind, any tiny amount forbids. Different kinds forbid only if the taste comes through.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns its examples into one general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine and water were only examples. The real rule is about kinds: מין במינו forbids במשהו, and שלא במינו forbids only בנותן טעם.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
A substance mixed with its own kind
In the smallest amount
Mixed with a different kind

steps.whatToRemember: For יין נסך: same kind forbids במשהו (any amount). A different kind forbids only בנותן טעם (if you can taste it).

phrases.english: This is the principle:
a substance with its own kind — in any amount;
and with a different kind — only when it imparts flavor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the examples in the previous step into one general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מין במינו forbids במשהו; שלא במינו forbids only בנותן טעם.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a stream of יין נסך poured into a cistern is nullified bit by bit
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports in the name of רבי יוחנן: if someone pours יין נסך from a barrel into a cistern, even all day, each bit is nullified as it falls in.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if a person pours forbidden wine from a barrel into a cistern, even all day long, each little bit that goes in is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ruling from רבי יוחנן, brought by רב דימי. A thin stream of forbidden wine falling into a large cistern of kosher wine is nullified piece by piece.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that at each moment only a tiny bit of forbidden wine enters, and the large amount of kosher wine cancels it right away. So even after pouring all day, the forbidden wine never builds up to forbid the cistern. This looks like it clashes with the משנה's rule that wine in wine forbids in any amount.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
One who pours
Cistern or pit holding wine
Each first bit is nullified as it comes in

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יוחנן is just repeating the משנה. The משנה said wine in wine forbids in any amount, yet רבי יוחנן says this stream is nullified. The גמרא will need to explain how these fit together.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
When Rav Dimi came,
he said that Rabbi Yochanan says:
One who pours libation wine
from a barrel into a cistern,
even all day long —
each first bit is nullified, one after another.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an אמורא's ruling about pouring יין נסך, which seems to limit the משנה's 'any amount' rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stream of יין נסך poured into a cistern of kosher wine is nullified bit by bit, even if the pouring goes on all day.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the 'any amount' rule for same-kind mixtures has a limit when the forbidden wine enters little by little.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: any amount of יין נסך forbids
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that יין נסך forbids a mixture in any amount. It suggests this means forbidden wine falling into permitted wine, which would clash with רב דימי's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: יין נסך is forbidden and forbids in any amount. Isn't that talking about forbidden wine falling into permitted wine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב דימי's rule from the previous step by quoting the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי said that forbidden wine poured into a pit of permitted wine is nullified little by little. The משנה says even a tiny bit of יין נסך forbids the mixture. If the משנה means forbidden wine falling into permitted wine, the two clash head-on.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden itself, and it makes other things forbidden
In any amount, even the smallest
Isn't it that...? (a suggestion that sets up a challenge)

phrases.english: We learned: יין נסך is forbidden
and forbids in any amount.
Isn't it talking about where
the forbidden fell into the permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: יֵין נֶסֶךְ אָסוּר וְאוֹסֵר בְּכׇל שֶׁהוּא. מַאי לָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב דימי's report in step 4 using the משנה from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's rule that each bit of יין נסך is nullified as it falls into permitted wine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה's 'forbids in any amount' means forbidden falling into permitted, then tiny amounts are not nullified, which contradicts רב דימי.

steps.title: The משנה means permitted falling into forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about permitted wine falling into forbidden wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is talking about the permitted falling into the forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב דימי by reading the משנה as describing the opposite direction of pouring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Which liquid falls into which makes all the difference. When permitted wine falls into forbidden wine, the forbidden wine is there first and is never 'swallowed up,' so it forbids everything. רב דימי's bit-by-bit nullifying only works when the forbidden is the one falling in.

keyTerms.meaning: No (rejecting the suggested reading)
The permitted into the forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: The direction of pouring matters. Forbidden falling into permitted can be nullified bit by bit. Permitted falling into forbidden is not.

phrases.english: No, it is where
the permitted fell into the forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּקָא נָפֵיל הֶתֵּירָא לְגוֹ אִיסּוּרָא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means forbidden wine fell into permitted wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means permitted wine fell into forbidden wine, so it does not clash with רב דימי.

steps.title: Second challenge: wine in water forbids by taste
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the next line of the משנה, wine in water forbids by taste. It suggests this means forbidden wine in permitted water, which again would not fit bit-by-bit nullifying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: wine in water forbids if it gives taste. Isn't that forbidden wine falling into permitted water?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to רב דימי from the next part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If forbidden wine poured into permitted water forbids once it adds taste, then the wine is not being nullified little by little as it falls in. That would go against רב דימי.

keyTerms.meaning: When it gives taste to the mixture
Wine (Aramaic)
Water (Aramaic)

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: יַיִן בְּמַיִם — בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם.
phrases.english: Come and hear: wine in water — when it gives taste.
Isn't it talking about where
forbidden wine fell into permitted water?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: יַיִן בְּמַיִם — בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב דימי, from the next clause of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forbidden wine falling into permitted water still forbids by taste, so it is not nullified as it falls.

steps.title: Wine in water means permitted wine into forbidden water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers again by flipping the case: permitted wine fell into forbidden water.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is talking about permitted wine falling into forbidden water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same kind of answer: the forbidden liquid was there first, and the permitted one fell into it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the water is the forbidden part, and the wine is permitted. Since the permitted wine falls into the forbidden water, רב דימי's rule about forbidden falling into permitted does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden water

phrases.english: No, it is where
permitted wine fell into forbidden water.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּקָא נָפֵיל חַמְרָא דְּהֶתֵּירָא לְמַיָּא דְּאִיסּוּרָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case (which liquid is forbidden, and direction of mixing)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forbidden wine fell into permitted water.
steps.terutzMaskana: Permitted wine fell into forbidden water.

steps.title: Challenge from the second half: water in wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if the first clause is about forbidden water, the second clause should be about forbidden water too. Then 'water in wine' would be forbidden water falling into permitted wine and forbidding by taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since the first clause is about forbidden water, the last clause should also be about forbidden water. Yet the last clause teaches: water in wine forbids when it gives taste!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the previous answer by saying the two halves of the משנה should be read the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both clauses are about forbidden water, then 'water in wine' means forbidden water falling into permitted wine. That is forbidden falling into permitted, and it still forbids by taste instead of being nullified bit by bit. So the problem for רב דימי comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה
The last clause of a משנה
And since... (sets up a reasoning from one part to another)

phrases.english: And since the first clause is about forbidden water,
the last clause is also about forbidden water,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: מַיִם בְּיַיִן — בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם!
phrases.english: and the last clause teaches: water in wine — when it gives taste!
phrases.notes: Read this way, forbidden water falls into permitted wine and still forbids. That is forbidden into permitted again.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּרֵישָׁא בְּמַיָּא דְּאִיסּוּרָא, סֵיפָא נָמֵי בְּמַיָּא דְּאִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 8 by demanding a consistent reading of both clauses.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 8 that the first clause is about forbidden water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A consistent reading makes the last clause a case of forbidden falling into permitted that forbids by taste, which goes against רב דימי.

steps.title: The whole משנה is permitted falling into forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי would answer that the whole משנה shares one feature: permitted falling into forbidden. The first clause is permitted wine into forbidden water. The last clause is permitted water into forbidden wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי can tell you: the whole משנה is about permitted falling into forbidden. The first clause is permitted wine falling into forbidden water. The last clause is permitted water falling into forbidden wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב דימי by showing that a different shared feature ties both clauses together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What the two clauses share is the direction, permitted falling into forbidden, and not which liquid is forbidden. So neither clause is about forbidden falling into permitted, and רב דימי's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you (an answer given on someone's behalf)
The entire משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The whole משנה is about permitted falling into forbidden, so רב דימי's rule about forbidden falling into permitted (nullified bit by bit) is never contradicted.

phrases.english: רב דימי can say to you:
the entire משנה is permitted into forbidden,
and the first clause is where
permitted wine fell into forbidden water,
the last clause is where
permitted water fell into forbidden wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב דִּימִי: כּוּלָּהּ מַתְנִיתִין הֶתֵּירָא לְגוֹ אִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the consistency challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different shared feature for both clauses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses must be about forbidden water.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both clauses share the direction (permitted into forbidden), while the forbidden liquid changes from clause to clause.

steps.title: רב יצחק בר יוסף's version: from a small canteen
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף reports רבי יוחנן's rule with a detail: the יין נסך is poured from a small canteen into a pit, and each bit is nullified even if he pours all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יצחק בר יוסף came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: one who pours יין נסך from a small canteen into a pit, even all day long, each first bit is nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report of רבי יוחנן's rule arrives, and it mentions a small canteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי's version in step 4 spoke of a barrel. This version speaks of a small canteen. That difference sets up the next line, which explains why the size matters.

keyTerms.meaning: When (a sage) came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
A small canteen or jug with a narrow opening
A pit or cistern of wine
Each bit is nullified as it comes in

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: When רב יצחק בר יוסף came,
he said that רבי יוחנן said:
one who pours יין נסך
from a small canteen into a pit,
even the whole day long —
each first bit is nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different report of the same רבי יוחנן rule that רב דימי reported in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יין נסך poured from a small canteen into a pit of permitted wine is nullified bit by bit, even if pouring continues all day.

steps.title: Only a small canteen, not a barrel
steps.stepSummary: The rule applies only to a small canteen, whose stream is thin. It does not apply to a barrel, whose stream is thick.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is only a small canteen, whose stream is not big. But a barrel, whose stream is big, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The text explains that the small canteen is a real condition of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thin stream is swallowed up right away, so each bit is nullified as it lands. A thick stream from a barrel counts as a real amount of forbidden wine, so it is not nullified bit by bit. This disagrees with רב דימי's version, which applied the rule even to a barrel.

keyTerms.meaning: Specifically, only this case
Its stream (literally, its column of liquid)
Big, significant
A barrel

steps.whatToRemember: By this version, bit-by-bit nullifying works only with a thin stream (a small canteen), not with a thick stream (a barrel).
steps.whyThisMatters: It narrows רבי יוחנן's rule. Whether the forbidden wine is nullified depends on how much pours in at once.

phrases.english: And specifically a small canteen,
whose stream is not big,
but a barrel, whose stream is big — no.
phrases.notes: This is the opposite of רב דימי's version in step 4, which said even a barrel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדַוְקָא צַרְצוּר קָטָן, דְּלָא נְפִישׁ עַמּוּדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the small canteen in step 11 matters and limits the rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bit-by-bit nullifying applies only to a thin stream such as from a small canteen, not to the thick stream of a barrel.

steps.title: רבין's report: water can nullify forbidden wine in a wine pit
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports in the name of רבי יוחנן: if יין נסך falls into a pit of permitted wine and a pitcher of water also falls in, we ignore the permitted wine. If the water is more than the forbidden wine, the water nullifies it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: forbidden libation wine fell into a pit of wine, and a pitcher of water also fell in. We look at the permitted wine as if it is not there. As for the rest, the water is more than the forbidden wine and cancels it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רבי יוחנן about forbidden wine that ends up in a pit holding both permitted wine and water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally wine in wine is never nullified, even by a lot of permitted wine. Here we pretend the permitted wine is not there and compare only the water to the forbidden wine. Water is a different kind, so if there is more water it cancels the forbidden wine.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing a teaching)
Wine poured for עבודה זרה, which is forbidden
A pitcher or jug
We view the permitted part as if it isn't there
They nullify (cancel out the forbidden item)

steps.confusionAlert: In 'מים רבין עליו', the word רבין means 'are more than'. It is not the name of the חכם רבין who opens this step.

phrases.english: When Ravin came
he said that Rabbi Yochanan says:
Libation wine that fell into a pit,
phrases.notes: The pit is full of permitted wine.

phrases.english: and a pitcher of water fell there too
we view the permitted wine as if it is not there,
and as for the rest, the water is more than it
phrases.notes: 'The rest' is the forbidden wine, and 'רבין' here just means 'are more'.

phrases.english: and nullifies it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about nullifying יין נסך with water, after the discussion of the canteen and the barrel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When water is also in the pit, we ignore the permitted wine. If the water is more than the forbidden wine, it nullifies the forbidden wine.

steps.title: The rule works only if the water fell in first
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יהודה reports that רבי יוחנן limited the rule: it works only if the water fell in first. If not, the forbidden wine joins the permitted wine and 'wakes up'.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב שמואל בר יהודה came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: this was taught only when the pitcher of water fell in first. If the water did not fall in first, the forbidden wine found its own kind and was strengthened.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report of רבי יוחנן adds a condition to the rule in רבין's report: the water must be in the pit before the forbidden wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the forbidden wine lands in pure wine first, it is wine in wine, so it forbids all the wine around it. Now the forbidden wine is much bigger, and the water that comes later is not enough to cancel it. Only if the water was already there do we skip the permitted wine and compare water to forbidden wine.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when... (a phrase that limits a rule)
First, beforehand
The kind found its own kind and was 'awakened', meaning it grew stronger and cannot be nullified

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: When Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda came,
he said that Rabbi Yochanan says:
They taught this only
where the pitcher of water fell in first,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא נָפַל שָׁם קִיתוֹן שֶׁל מַיִם תְּחִלָּה
phrases.english: but if a pitcher of water did not fall there first
the kind found its own kind and was awakened.
phrases.notes: The forbidden wine met permitted wine, made it all forbidden, and became too big for the water to cancel.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבין's rule to a case where the water fell in first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The water nullifies the forbidden wine only if it fell into the pit before the forbidden wine.

steps.title: A second version places the rule on the משנה
steps.stepSummary: Some attach רב שמואל בר יהודה's teaching to the משנה's rule that wine in wine forbids in any amount. In this version, that rule does not apply if a pitcher of water fell there, and nothing is said about which fell first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this on the משנה: 'Wine in wine forbids in any amount.' רב שמואל בר יהודה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: this was taught only when no pitcher of water fell there. But if a pitcher of water fell there, we view the permitted wine as if it is not there, and the water, which is more than the forbidden wine, nullifies it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the same teaching, attached to a line of the משנה instead of to רבין's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the teaching is an exception to the משנה's harsh rule that wine in wine is never nullified. It says the exception applies whenever water fell there, with no mention of order. This sets up the question in the next step about what difference the two versions make.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (a different version of where a teaching belongs)
On our משנה
Any amount at all, even the smallest

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on our Mishnah:
Wine in wine forbids in any amount.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda said that Rabbi Yochanan says:
They taught this only

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא נָפַל שָׁם קִיתוֹן שֶׁל מַיִם,
phrases.english: where a pitcher of water did not fall there,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נָפַל שָׁם קִיתוֹן שֶׁל מַיִם
phrases.english: but if a pitcher of water fell there
we view the permitted wine as if it is not there,
and as for the rest, the water is more than it
and nullifies it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב שמואל בר יהודה's teaching, attached to the משנה instead of to רבין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's rule that wine in wine forbids in any amount does not apply when water fell there. Then the water, if it is more, nullifies the forbidden wine.

steps.title: What difference do the two versions make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the practical difference between attaching the teaching to the משנה and attaching it to רבין's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between the one who teaches it on the משנה and the one who teaches it on רבין's statement?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to set up its next move: what changes depending on which version we follow?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling sounds the same in both versions, since water can nullify forbidden wine. So the גמרא wants to know what practical case is decided differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between...?
On רבין's statement

phrases.english: What difference is there between
the one who teaches it on the Mishnah,
and the one who teaches it on Ravin's statement?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין לִדְמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַמַּתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two versions just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between the two versions of the teaching.

steps.title: The difference: whether the water must fall in first
steps.stepSummary: In the version on the משנה, the water does not need to fall in first. In the version on רבין's statement, it must fall in first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who teaches it on the משנה does not need the water to come first. The one who teaches it on רבין's statement needs the water to come first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two versions differ on one point: does it matter whether the water or the forbidden wine fell in first?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Attached to רבין, the teaching adds a condition to his rule, so the water must come first. Attached to the משנה, it is simply an exception to 'wine in wine', so any water there can nullify the forbidden wine, whatever the order.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not require
Requires

steps.whatToRemember: Water can nullify יין נסך in a wine pit because we ignore the permitted wine. In the version on רבין, the water must fall in first. In the version on the משנה, the order does not matter.

phrases.english: The one who teaches it on the Mishnah
does not need the water to fall in first,
and the one who teaches it on Ravin's statement
needs the water to fall in first.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַמַּתְנִיתִין לָא בָּעֵי תְּחִלָּה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The version on the משנה does not require the water to fall in first. The version on רבין's statement does require it.

steps.title: Setting up the case of forbidden wine and water falling into a pit
steps.stepSummary: With the word איתמר, the גמרא introduces a new case. יין נסך fell into a pit, and a pitcher of water also fell in.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: if יין נסך fell into a pit, and a pitcher of water also fell there,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new report with איתמר and describing a case. This line only sets things up. The rulings about the case come in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of case as רבין's report in the name of רבי יוחנן: forbidden wine and water both end up in the pit. The new question is how to rule when both fall in. So far the גמרא has only described the case, not given an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A pit or cistern. Here it is a pit that holds wine.
A pitcher of water.
Fell in, meaning it got mixed in without anyone meaning to do it.

phrases.english: It was stated: libation wine that fell into a pit,
phrases.notes: The pit here is full of permitted wine, so the forbidden wine is now mixed in with it.

phrases.english: and a pitcher of water fell there,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new reported discussion about the forbidden wine and water case that רבין raised in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only describes the case: יין נסך and a pitcher of water both fell into a pit of wine.
